correctness.rationale: On Petersen P=KG(5,2), independently enumerated all 1024 induced subsets: B(P) of bipartite induced graphs has 806 faces including empty and F(P) of induced forests has 786. The 20 difference faces are exactly 10 induced 6-cycles and 10 distinct 7-vertex cofaces, each six-cycle face in precisely one B coface; hence these ten free codimension-one pairs collapse B onto F. Independently reconstructed full F poset and greedy discrete Morse matching, obtaining 389 matched pairs, 7 critical faces (one 0-cell and six 5-cells) and verifying acyclicity by topological sorting all 3,470 oriented Hasse incidences; thus F≃∨⁶S⁵ integrally. Checked all 120 permutations of the five letters preserve each pair set and independently computed signed fixed-face traces; their fifth homology character distribution is 6 (1), −2 (15), 0 (80), 1 (24), precisely ∧² of the standard 4-dimensional S5 module, inner-product one. This is exhaustive for the ten-vertex graph and proves the exact finite statement, not a claim about all graphs.

originality.rationale: QUALIFIED PASS. Grady–Knoll–Laskar–Lipman introduce odd-cycle-independent and cycle-independent vertex-set conditions; Carnero Bravo studies forest filtrations for paths, cycles and related families. The previously published S5 representation ∧²V for ordinary Petersen three-cut Δ₃(P), read in full, concerns a DIFFERENT graph complex and does not imply a collapse B(P)↘F(P); the equality of representation is not enough to identify a chain inclusion or simple-homotopy pairing. The forest homotopy/character and Petersen induced hexagon count are prior or contextual; the distinctive claimed finding is the ten free-pair S5-invariant comparison. A historical signed Petersen graph equivalence remains possible.
residual_risks: Previously published Petersen forest homotopy and homology character must not be misrepresented as novel; novelty is solely the inclusion/collapse.
Historical odd-cycle hitting-set or signed-Petersen literature may use an equivalent complex under a different name.
The collection of collapse pairs is S5-invariant; this does not assert that each sequential elementary deletion is individually S5-equivariant.

value.rationale: The precise equivariant collection of elementary collapses gives a canonical comparison of two independently motivated hereditary graph complexes and proves that allowing induced even cycles adds no homotopy in this canonical graph. Its exact ten-pair inclusion certificate is usable independently even though the constituent wedge type and representation were known. It is a concrete nontrivial simple-homotopy bridge, not merely a recomputed face count.
